excludes: General frontend feature implementation is owned by frontend-implement.
Broad accessibility remediation is owned by accessibility-implement.
Screenshot-baseline infrastructure is owned by visual-regression.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement purposeful UI animation and enter/leave lifecycle with installed capability, reduced-motion equivalence, CSP-safe code, interruption cleanup and measured performance.

provenance.claim_scope: Angular animations deprecation and migration from 20.2
Angular animate enter and leave lifecycle

reference_routing.prompt: A pinned Angular application must decide whether to retain legacy triggers or migrate a component to animate.enter and animate.leave while preserving leave completion and test behavior.
A React project already pins Motion and needs keyed presence, layout continuity and interruption-safe reduced motion for a swapping panel.
An installed GSAP timeline coordinates a complex scroll sequence and must clean all triggers on route change, honor runtime reduced motion and keep strict CSP.
A pinned SvelteKit list needs keyed reorder and enter/leave transitions whose reduced-motion path preserves outro removal and navigation cleanup.
Add a progressively enhanced same-document route transition with unique names, failure and rapid-navigation handling, stable history/focus and an unsupported-browser fallback.
A Vue TransitionGroup list needs named-property CSS transitions, stable keys, cancellation cleanup and correct reduced-motion completion under rapid reorder.
Handle a routine animation motion request using the main workflow only; no framework, library, image, navigation, table, utility, or other optional deep dive is needed.

risk.rationale: animation-motion implements repository behavior; edits remain limited to the authorized scope and require affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Implement a new interactive frontend workflow with components, routes, data fetching, forms, authorization states and error handling; motion is incidental.
Repair keyboard navigation, form semantics, headings, live announcements, focus management, contrast and reduced-motion defects across a user flow.

positive.prompt: Migrate one Angular component's legacy enter/leave animation on an installed line that supports the new compiler primitives, preserving reduced-motion removal, focus, callbacks and tests without mixing systems in the component.
Implement a capability-gated route transition with identical URL/history/focus/final DOM fallback, safe interruption, reduced motion, unique transition names and CSP that forbids unsafe evaluation.

assertions.criterion: Implements motion and lifecycle behavior without implementing or claiming ownership of general feature work, broad accessibility remediation or visual-baseline infrastructure.
Inspects installed framework/library, motion tokens, component lifecycle, CSP, SSR/hydration, browser targets, preferences and tests from the fixture.
Defines before/during/after state, interruption and reduced-motion final state, selects the smallest installed capability, names properties and then implements independent cleanup/completion.

Eliminates transition all and evaluated code, preserves strict CSP, keeps reduced-motion lifecycle equivalent and on Angular 20.2-or-later capability uses or plans migration to animate.enter/leave without mixing legacy systems in one component.

Tests enter/leave/reversal, rapid toggles, unmount, focus/pointer, reduced preference before and during runtime, SSR/hydration, unsupported capability, CSP and measured layout/paint/composite behavior.
Reports purpose/lifecycle, selected reference and capability, named properties/tokens, reduced-motion fallback, tests/performance/CSP evidence and residual risk.
Uses repository motion tokens, scoped cleanup and capability adapters rather than universal timings, global hacks or framework recipes copied from memory.

scenarios.prompt: An app uses transition: all, string-evaluated animation callbacks that require unsafe-eval CSP, and a global near-zero-duration reduced-motion rule. Exit cleanup waits on animationend, so nodes remain inert or mounted. Angular code also copies deprecated legacy APIs into a capable new project. Repair it.

assertions.criterion: Stops coupling a destructive mutation to animation completion and refuses CSP weakening; resolves mutation ownership, exact lifecycle, cancellation, focus and rollback before changing motion.
Moves business state to an explicit authorized/idempotent path, keeps animation presentation-only and guarantees the same final DOM/callback state under reduced motion, error and interruption.
Requires persisted mutation outcome plus normal/reduced/interrupted lifecycle and strict-CSP evidence rather than visual disappearance.

scenarios.prompt: A production modal's destructive action is triggered after its exit animation; reduced-motion users skip that callback, while a proposed fix enables unsafe-eval for a timeline library. Explain the safe boundary.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives authority from the lockfile, installed Angular/compiler types and browser support; retains compatible legacy behavior for the pin, capability-gates View Transitions and treats migration separately. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks framework/compiler, animation library, runtime/browser, SSR adapter, CSP and test environment together.
Documents the installed capability/migration seam and avoids remembered removal dates, browser claims or latest-only syntax.

scenarios.prompt: A repository pins Angular below the line that exposes animate.enter/leave, but current documentation marks @angular/animations deprecated; another browser lacks the selected View Transition capability. No upgrade is authorized.
